Story Map: Author and Editor (Triage and Routing)

The story maps follow the empathy journeys on slides 7 and 8 of the Group-16 Design Thinking deck (Content Creation, Content Curation and Content Delivery): a named persona, three themed lanes, and three steps that take the persona from today’s pain point to the outcome. Each card is an activity the working prototype supports today. Below each journey, the classic story map lists the backbone activities with the user stories under them, marked GreenBUILT (in the working prototype) or GreyNEXT (MVP) (next release).

Persona 1: Author

Persona

Goal

Pain points today

Needs

Dr. Priya Nair, a postdoctoral chemist in her early 30s, preparing a manuscript for JACS

Submit a manuscript that is accepted for review the first time, in the right journal

  • Journal rules and templates are spread across sites

  • Problems surface only at desk review, weeks later

  • No view of how well the MSC fits the journal

  • Little visibility of status once submitted

  • A journal-specific template and guidelines

  • An objective score with clear fixes before submitting

  • A fit score and a better-fit journal if needed

  • Status, decision and feedback in one place

Persona 2: Editor (Triage and Routing)

Persona

Goal

Pain points today

Needs

Mark Ellis, an Associate Editor in his 40s who triages 40+ new MSCs a week across several journals

Route every new MSC to the right reviewer quickly and reach a defensible decision on time

  • No single view of integrity, fit and age of new MSCs

  • Reviewer availability is found by e-mail and memory

  • Invitations go unanswered without anyone noticing

  • Reading a whole MSC before deciding where it belongs

  • A prioritized dashboard with time-elapsed cues

  • Reviewer proposals by availability and expertise

  • Invitation status at a glance, with a quick recheck

  • An at-a-glance analysis: summary, integrity and fit

Design Thinking Point of View (POV)

The storyline follows the five Design Thinking levers used in the Group-16 deck (Empathize, Define, Ideate, Prototype, Test), applied here to manuscript submission and editorial triage instead of news consumption.

#EEF3FB

How might we reimagine manuscript submission, triage and routing so that Authors submit first-time-right manuscripts to the right journal, and Editors route each one to the right reviewer and decide faster, with evidence?

Stage

Author

Editor (Triage and Routing)

Where it shows on this page

1. Empathize

Priya spends weeks on a manuscript, then learns at desk review that it misses journal rules or belongs in another journal. The rules are scattered and the feedback arrives late.

Mark faces a queue of new MSCs with no single view of their integrity, fit or age. Reviewer availability lives in e-mail threads, and unanswered invitations stall MSCs unnoticed.

Persona tables and the pain-point cards on Figures SM-1 and SM-2

2. Define

POV: Priya, a time-pressed early-career Author, needs an objective check of her MSC against the journal’s rules before she submits, because late desk rejects cost weeks and confidence.

POV: Mark, a high-volume Editor, needs one prioritized view of every MSC with its integrity, fit and reviewer status, because routing by memory and e-mail delays decisions and hides bottlenecks.

The How Might We statement above

3. Ideate

  • Journal-specific templates and guidelines

  • Automated integrity score with How to fix

  • Journal fitment index and transfer path

  • Self-service status and revision upload

  • Prioritized dashboard with time-elapsed cues

  • Availability-based reviewer proposals

  • Invitation workflow with status recheck

  • MSC Analysis to triage without reading everything

  • Highlight palette to tag findings by type

Backbone activities and user stories in the story map tables

4. Prototype

Working prototype Author view: journal dropdown with cover, template download, organized MSC preview, 1-10 integrity score with PASS above 6, journal fit, My submissions and revisions.

Working prototype Editor view: dashboard with tabs, KPIs and filters, reviewer modal and invitation e-mails with the refresh icon, Review and Annotate page with MSC Analysis and the 6-colour palette, five decisions including Assign to PE, spinner and Usage Metrics.

Functional Specifications above (items marked GreenNEW and BlueUPDATED) and the live prototype at unified-editorial-platform.onrender.com

5. Test

  • Walk-throughs with Authors using the pass / fail sample MSCs

  • Measure: % first-time PASS, re-checks per MSC, desk-reject rate

  • Ask: are the How to fix hints clear and the fit % trusted?

  • Walk-throughs with Editors on the ~50 seeded open MSCs

  • Measure: time to reviewer acceptance, % MSCs in green, time to decision

  • Ask: does MSC Analysis agree with the reviewer’s own judgement?

Usage Metrics and the audit trail record each session and action; the API smoke test (npm test) covers the Author and Editor flows. Findings feed the next iteration of the story map.
